title: One tip vocabulary for every lab
summary: A single change to src/content/lab/tips.ts that adds every field, phase, route and event the four group plans asked for, with their naming conflicts resolved, so that no later package edits the vocabulary. Merges the vocabulary parts of pci-tip-vocabulary, diag-tip-context, proc-tip-context and tips-procedure-vocabulary, and the events that diag-route-arch-femoral-variants and diag-grafts-arterial would have added.
tipIntegration: Defines what every lab reports. LabContext gains phases?: LabPhase[] (matched as a union with phase; used by the full case to report step and site together), procedures?: LabProcedure[], technique?, step?: number and imaging?: 'ivus'|'oct'. TipTrigger gains procedure?: LabProcedure[], technique?: BifTechnique[], step?: [from,to] and imaging?. Each must match when the trigger sets it; scoring adds technique +3, step +2, imaging +2, procedure +2. LabTip gains alsoIn?: { lab: LabId; phase?: LabPhase[] }[] so a tip written for one lab can appear in another at named phases of the borrowing lab. tipsForAll(ctxs, limit) merges per-context results, dedups by id and keeps score order. ACCESS_ROUTES adds distal-radial, ulnar, femoral-vein, jugular, subclavian. LAB_PHASES.bedside becomes assess, access, position, test, troubleshoot, decide, plan, needle, drain, with the old 'pacing' and 'pericardiocentesis' kept as deprecated aliases until found-tip-retarget removes them. LAB_PROCEDURES = tavi, bav, teer, tteer, transseptal, laao, septal-occluder, pmc, septal-ablation, iabp, impella, ecmo, large-bore, pacing, tcp, overdrive, biopsy, pericardiocentesis.
lessonAndCaseLinks: None. Lesson tip blocks render through TIP_BY_ID and are unaffected.
design: Naming decisions (binding for all packages): (1) Case and scenario properties are events raised for the whole case and gated with requires; there is no separate flags field (the diagnostic plan's TipTrigger.flags and CASE_FLAGS are dropped). (2) CTO is 'cto' (no 'chronic-occlusion'); ostial lesions are 'aorto-ostial-lesion' or 'branch-ostial-lesion'; in-stent lesions are 'in-stent-lesion' (not 'isr'); SCAD is 'scad-suspected' (not 'scad'); complete heart block is 'av-block' (not 'heart-block'); ventricular tachycardia is 'vt'; atrial fibrillation is 'atrial-fibrillation' (not 'af'); collateral perforation is 'perforation-collateral'; a pseudolesion is 'new-narrowing-tortuous'; a wire in a wrong arch or access branch is 'wire-misdirected' (not 'wire-wrong-branch'); route resistance is 'wire-resistance' (not 'iliac-resistance'). New LAB_EVENTS, grouped with comments: lesion and scenario (raised for the whole case): left-main-lesion, graft-lesion, in-stent-lesion, scad-suspected, calcified-lesion, stent-thrombosis, small-vessel, large-vessel, long-lesion, prior-cabg, post-arrest, prior-tavi, stemi, nste-acs, high-flow, contrast-sensitive, no-onsite-pci, pregnancy-possible, pde5-recent, vasopressor; haemodynamic scenario flags: aortic-stenosis, low-flow-aortic-stenosis, mitral-stenosis, hocm, constriction, restriction, pulmonary-embolism, pulmonary-hypertension, tricuspid-regurgitation, tricuspid-stenosis, pulmonary-stenosis, atrial-shunt, ventricular-shunt, cardiogenic-shock, tamponade; patient: vt, atrial-fibrillation, av-block, vagal, lv-ectopy, pericardial-effusion, pulmonary-oedema, high-lvedp, desaturation, over-sedation, neuro-deficit; PCI equipment and technique: wire-fracture, balloon-entrapment, balloon-no-deflate, balloon-rupture, stent-loss-wire-out, snare-in-use, extension-in-place, epd-deployed, wire-out-of-guide, second-wire-with-device; flow: no-reflow-refractory, plaque-embolisation; calcium: atherectomy-rotational, atherectomy-orbital, burr-not-advancing, burr-deceleration, long-run, laser-active, ivl-active; perforation: perforation-large-vessel, perforation-distal, perforation-collateral; CTO: retrograde, retrograde-connection; diagnostic: vasodilator-given, operator-dose-alarm, wire-in-lv, wire-not-leading, aspiration-failed, catheter-plugged, transducer-fault, contrast-hold-up, myocardial-stain, papillary-entrapment, catheter-induced-regurgitation, non-diagnostic-run, territory-unsupplied, graft-stump, subclavian-stenosis, torque-not-transmitted; access: wire-resistance, wire-misdirected, wrong-height, dilator-resistance, act-high, pseudoaneurysm; devices: catheter-knot, suction, pump-migration, ventilated. Types BifTechnique ('provisional'|'dk-crush'|'culotte'|'t-stent'|'tap'|'reverse-crush'|'mini-crush'|'v-stent'|'sks'), ImagingModality and LabProcedure. validate.ts (validateTips): step only with technique and from <= to; imaging and procedure values from their lists; alsoIn phases must belong to LAB_PHASES of the borrowing lab. tipsFor keeps its behaviour for contexts that set only phase (the diagnostic and PCI labs today).
acceptance: vitest content.test.ts and manual.test.ts pass unchanged (no tip is retargeted here)
tips.test.ts: a snapshot of tipsFor for 20 existing diagnostic and PCI contexts (phase only) is identical before and after
tips.test.ts: validateTips rejects step without technique, an unknown procedure, and alsoIn with a phase that is not in the borrowing lab
tips.test.ts: tipsForAll over an access and a diagnostic context returns each tip once, highest score first

title: Retarget the lesson tips the early labs can raise, and report reachability
summary: The edits to the when: triggers of tips in src/content/manual/** that narrow a tip to its lab, procedure, route or scenario using names the labs raise by the end of phase 1, done in one pass because they touch the same module files. No caution or bailout tip leaves a complication context the PCI lab reports (superset test). Every other requested retarget is recorded as data in waiting.ts for tip-retarget-catchup and content-links-backfill-p2. Adds the reachability test, which reads what each lab raises from the event sources themselves. Merges the retargeting parts of pci-tip-vocabulary, tips-procedure-vocabulary, proc-tip-context, proc-consent-conversation, diag-tip-context, diag-radiation-practice and diag-acs-scenarios.
tipIntegration: Only trigger objects change; titles, text, sources and lesson ids do not. Rule for this package: an edit is applied here only when every name it gates on or moves to is raised by the tip's lab no later than phase 1, or when the tip's lab shows no tips today (only the diagnostic and PCI labs do). Applied here. PCI: CTO tips that list 'total-occlusion' move to requires ['cto']; bifurcation tips that are not technique-specific gain requires ['bifurcation']; calcium tips that are not device-specific gain requires ['calcified-lesion']; ostial tips gain requires aorto-ostial-lesion or branch-ostial-lesion, and pci-ostial-rota-coaxial, pci-ostial-undilatable and pci-ostial-stent-underexpanded move back to lesion-prep or optimise; the pm-imaging lesion-type tips (pci-img-ct-cap, pci-img-ostial-coverage, pci-img-scad-caution) gain the matching lesion requires; OCT tips move to imaging 'oct'; pci-ocx-* and diag-ocx-* gain requires on in-stent-lesion, scad-suspected, stent-thrombosis, small-vessel, large-vessel or long-lesion as their text demands. Haemo tips listed in hb-specific-conditions#9 gain requires on their scenario flag. Every structural-* and mcs-* tip gains a procedure (structural-ts-* get ['transseptal']; mcs-largebore-*, mcs-preclose-* and mcs-cx-crossover-* get ['large-bore','impella','ecmo','iabp']; mcs-select-* get all three devices); the bed-peri-* tips move from phase 'pericardiocentesis' to procedure ['pericardiocentesis'] plus their stage phase. Access: access-central-vein-no-blood to { phase ['puncture'], event ['no-flashback'], route ['jugular','subclavian'] }; access-femoral-vein-redirect to { phase ['femoral'], event ['venous-flashback'], route ['femoral'] }; access-root-aneurysm-suspect, access-femoral-sheath-act, access-planning-closure-infection and access-artery-vein-same-groin gain route femoral. Diagnostic: diag-planning-ad-hoc-consent to phase ['setup','finish']; diag-ohca-ecg-sorts gains requires ['post-arrest']; the 32 pci, access, haemo and structural tips the diagnostic requests cite gain alsoIn [{ lab: 'diagnostic', phase: [...] }] with the diagnostic phase each belongs to. Recorded in waiting.ts, not applied (each entry holds the tip id, its new trigger and the package that raises the names it needs): the perforation tips to perforation-large-vessel, perforation-distal and perforation-collateral (pci-perforation); the 24 bifurcation technique tips to technique and step (pci-bifurcation-provisional, pci-bifurcation-two-stent); pci-calc-rota-* to atherectomy-rotational and pci-calc-orbital-low-speed to atherectomy-orbital (pci-calcium-uncrossable); pci-gx-second-wire to extension-in-place (pci-device-delivery); the adrenaline line of pci-noreflow-pick-agent to no-reflow-refractory, pci-embol-plaque-aspirate to plaque-embolisation, pci-wire-spasm-nitrate to coronary-spasm and pci-interp-pseudolesion to new-narrowing (pci-flow-closure); retrograde tips to retrograde (pci-cto-retrograde); pci-wire-prolapse-four-solutions and pci-wire-reversed-hairpin to wire-prolapse, pci-wire-pseudolesion-pullback to new-narrowing-tortuous, pci-microcath-hydraulic-limits and pci-microcath-cannot-trap to microcatheter-removal, pci-wire-stop-at-guide-tip to wire-out-of-guide and pci-wire-load-through-valve to second-wire-with-device (pci-wire-microcatheter); pci-phys-ach-* to ach-provocation (physiology-anoca-cft); the bed-pace-* tips from phase 'pacing' to procedure ['pacing'] plus stage phase (pacing-in-lab-scenarios-and-tips); pci-wire-fracture-ivus-first to wire-fracture, pci-balloon-trap-in-guide to balloon-entrapment and pci-snare-* to snare-in-use (pci-equipment-loss, P2); pci-epd-* to epd-deployed (pci-graft, P2); pci-rad-operator-dose-alarm to operator-dose-alarm (diag-radiation-practice, P2). The deprecated 'pacing' and 'pericardiocentesis' phase aliases stay in LAB_PHASES until tip-retarget-catchup. The validator now requires a procedure on every structural, mcs and pericardiocentesis tip.
lessonAndCaseLinks: No link changes. Every lessonId stays valid (validateTips).
design: Mechanical edits by tip id. Before editing, grep each id and confirm the module file; record any id that does not exist in the PR notes rather than inventing one. Superset guard: before and after the edits the package computes, for the contexts the PCI lab reports today in lad-focal and rca-calcified (phase 'complication' with each of perforation, dissection, no-reflow, thrombus and air), the caution and bailout tips returned by tipsFor(ctx, 100); any edit that would remove one of them moves to waiting.ts instead of being applied. Reachability: src/content/lab/reachability.test.ts globs, with import.meta.glob({ eager: true, import: 'raises' }), the event sources and tip-context files of every lab (src/ui/lab/pciEvents/*.ts, src/ui/sim/modules/*.ts, src/simulation/session/modules/*.ts, src/ui/lab/*Context.ts and src/ui/**/*Tips.ts); a module without a raises export is skipped. raises is { lab, phases, events, techniques?, imaging?, procedures?, routes? }; for PCI event sources it is derived from the file's PCI_EVENT_SOURCES and the phases it sets, so the declaration cannot drift from the code. The test enumerates which tips are satisfiable and prints satisfiable, waiting and ready counts per lab. It fails only for a tip that is neither satisfiable nor listed in src/content/lab/raisable/waiting.ts. waiting.ts holds two kinds of entry, both keyed by the package expected to raise the names: tips waiting on their current trigger, and deferred retargets { tipId, when, raisedBy }; an entry whose names are now raised is reported 'ready', and a stale entry is a warning, not a failure. No package writes a hand-made list of what it raises; each exports raises from its own event source or tip-context file. Only found-tip-retarget, tip-retarget-catchup and content-links-backfill-p2 edit waiting.ts.

title: One deep-link shape for lessons, cases and every lab
summary: Lessons, cases, the case library and progress screens open any lab at a named scenario, variant, start state and mode through one parameter shape and one pending-launch store. Replaces four separate designs (PCI_LAUNCH_KEYS and requestPciLaunch, the diagnostic sim block scenario and seed fields, the full case's requestScenario, and the dev labs' preset and takeLabPreset). Adds a runtime practice index built from every scenario pack's .launch.ts, so each lesson and case lists the scenarios that practise it from the day the scenario lands.
tipIntegration: None directly. A launch may carry initial events (for example 'perforation' or 'prior-cabg') that the receiving lab adds to its context for the whole run.
lessonAndCaseLinks: Schema: the sim block becomes { kind:'sim', sim, task, params?: LaunchParams }, Module.sims and CaseStudy.sims gain params, and CaseStudy gains practice?: { sim, params?, task }[] rendered after the outcome as 'Practise this in the lab'. LaunchParams is Record<string,string> with standard keys scenario, variant, seed, start, mode (guided|supervised|independent|exam), technique, workspace, step, preset. Existing drill blocks with target 'angio-pci' are read the same way. useUiStore.openSim(sim, params) stores the request in useLabLaunchStore for every sim (angio-real keeps requestDrill); each lab calls takeLaunch(sim) on mount and on simTab change. Pending launches are never persisted in NavMemory. practiceIndex adds 'Practise this in the lab' entries under every lesson and case that a .launch.ts names, with no lesson edit.
design: New src/state/useLabLaunchStore.ts: request(sim, params), take(sim) returns the params once, peek(sim). New src/content/validateLaunch.ts: validateLaunchLinks(contentRoot, known) checks every sim block, module sim and case practice entry: the scenario id exists for that sim, start and variant ids belong to that scenario, mode is a known value, and a scenario marked heldOut is never linked from lessons or cases (exam integrity, HANDOVER 6.4). Known ids are passed in, not imported: content.test.ts builds them with import.meta.glob over src/**/*.launch.ts, engine-free metadata files that each lab's scenario packs export ({ sim, scenarios: [{ id, title, lessonIds, caseIds?, starts?, variants?, heldOut? }], links?: [{ scenario?, drill?, start?, variant?, mode?, lessonIds, caseIds? }] }). A links entry may point at a scenario declared in another file (merged by sim and scenario id) and may declare the start it adds, so a feature package that adds a start state or a drill writes its own src/content/practice/<package-id>.launch.ts instead of editing a pack it does not own. Practice index: src/ui/content/practiceIndex.ts globs src/**/*.launch.ts eagerly at runtime (src/content/manual/index.ts already globs the module files this way) and builds lessonId and caseId to { sim, scenario?, drill?, start?, variant?, mode, title } lists, excluding heldOut scenarios. BlockRenderer renders 'Practise this in the lab' under each lesson for every entry and CaseStudies.tsx does the same for each case, so a package's links appear the day its .launch.ts lands, without editing lesson files. Scripts that touch content run with vite-node, as scripts/content/status.ts already does ('npx vite-node scripts/content/status.ts'; it calls import.meta.glob itself on line 5); scripts/README.md records this. import.meta.glob is already typed for the app program (src/render/xray/realism.test.ts carries the vite/client reference and tsconfig.app.json includes src), so no vite-env.d.ts is added. BlockRenderer passes params; CaseStudies.tsx renders practice links. Registries by glob (a rule for every later package): runtime registries that many packages extend are discovered with import.meta.glob({ eager: true }) instead of a hand-edited index, so a package adds a file instead of editing a shared list. This applies to PCI scenario packs, PCI consoles, PCI device render modules, PCI input bindings, PCI event sources, diagnostic scenario packs and session modules, full-case scenarios, session modules, chart and order sections, table-side control tabs, mentor rule files, debrief sections and checks, physics implementations, dev-lab presets and practice link files.

title: Shared event log, patient-event adapter, tip panel, run logging, decision ledger and dev hooks
summary: The plumbing every lab needs to show tips and score a run: one event log with hold windows, one adapter from engine vitals to patient events, one tip hook and panel with the visibility policy, one run-logging API with case id, mode, decisions and metrics, one decision ledger, and window.__lab dev hooks for hidden-pane checks. Merges labs-tips-panel-and-session (dev), the LabEventLog (diagnostic), the EventLatch (PCI), the case tips panel visibility (full case) and the shared engine-event adapter the full-case plan asked for.
tipIntegration: src/ui/lab/eventLog.ts: EventLog with raise(event, holdS?), active(now), history() and a TRANSIENT_HOLD_S default of 30 s (a labelled model parameter) with per-event overrides; every raise is also written as 'lab.event' telemetry for the debrief. src/ui/lab/patientEvents.ts: patientEvents(vitals, prev) returns hypotension (MAP below 65 mmHg held 10 s; model parameter), bradycardia (HR below 50), vf, vt, atrial-fibrillation, av-block, st-elevation, chest-pain, contrast-reaction, desaturation, pulmonary-oedema, high-lvedp, pericardial-effusion, tamponade, low-act and high-contrast-volume from PatientEngine vitals; the diagnostic lab, the PCI lab, the full case and the physiology lab all use it, so patient tips appear in every lab. useContextTips(ctx | ctxs, policy) generalises useDiagnosticTips: lazy loadTips(), guided shows tips as they become relevant, supervised and independent after askHelp() (counted against entrustment), exam shows none.
lessonAndCaseLinks: Run rows carry caseId '<sim>:<scenario>[~variant]', so the logbook and debrief link back to the launch params.
design: New src/ui/lab/LabTipsPanel.tsx (collapsible, Clinical Graphite tokens, 'Ask for a tip', lesson link through openLesson, active events in a DEV-only row) and src/ui/lab/LabModeBar.tsx. New src/ui/lab/labRun.ts: useLabRun(sim, caseId, launchMode?) returns { mode, policy, helpAskedAt, askHelp, decide(rec), finish({ score, passed, criticalErrors, complications, metrics }) }; finish calls useProgressStore.logSession once per run with lab, source (the old simKey, so simKeyEpas still maps EPAs), caseId, scenarioId, mode, decisions and metrics. src/mentor/ledger.ts: DecisionRecord { id, t, stage, label, correct, expected, given, lessonId?, tipIds? } shared by the full case, the PCI sign-out, the diagnostic study report and the dev labs. src/progress/types.ts and useProgressStore gain the new LogSessionInput fields; recordSim stays for old callers. src/dev/labHooks.ts: registerLabHook(name, { context, tips, state, step? }) installs window.__lab[name] in DEV builds so labs that rely on requestAnimationFrame can be inspected and advanced while the pane is hidden. Policy comes from src/ui/lab/visibility.ts resolveLabPolicy, with the launch mode overriding the level-derived mode.

title: Shared lesion, graft, anatomy-variant and chart types
summary: One set of case-model types used by the diagnostic scenarios, the PCI scenario registry and the full case, so that a lesion means the same thing in every lab (the diagnostic plan's cross-cutting request) and src/types/index.ts is edited once instead of by eight packages.
tipIntegration: None directly. Lesion morphology and case chart fields are what labs turn into the scenario events of found-tips-vocabulary.
lessonAndCaseLinks: None.
design: Types only, with defaults that keep current cases unchanged. AnatomyVariant adds anomalous-lcx-right-sinus, anomalous-lcx-from-rca, anomalous-rca-left-sinus, anomalous-lm-right-sinus, high-ostia, conus-separate-ostium, myocardial-bridge, fistula-lad-pa, very-dilated-root, arteria-lusoria, iliac-stenosis, iliac-stent, iliac-occlusion, aortic-occlusion, aaa, tall-patient. Lesion gains optional eccentricity (0-1), orientationDeg, taperMm, branchAt, morphology ('concentric'|'thrombus'|'spasm'|'scad'|'cto'), nitrateResponsive, scadType ('1'|'2A'|'2B'|'3'), calcium (0-2), calciumArcDeg, thrombusGrade (0-5), lipid, sites (LabEvent subset), medina, sideBranch { vessel, angleDeg, diameterMm }, role ('target'|'non-culprit'|'bystander'), cto { stump: 'tapered'|'blunt', lengthMm, collaterals: CollateralChannel[] }. CollateralChannel { donor, recipient, type: 'septal'|'epicardial', wernerCC, rentrop, tortuosity }. Graft { conduit: 'svg'|'radial'|'lima'|'rima', target, position, proximalSite, status: 'patent'|'diseased'|'occluded', ringMarker, sequential? }. AnatomyCase gains scenarioId?, events? (case-wide LabEvents), chart?: CaseChart, grafts?: Graft[]. CaseChart: age, sex, heightCm, weightKg, creatinine and eGFR, echo (LVEF, valve disease), drugs with last-dose times, allergies, pregnancy status, prior fluoroscopic procedures and skin findings, operation note, arm pressures, arrest history, ECG id, consent scope, previous catheters that worked. The random case generator's variant pool is an explicit list, so the new variants never appear in random cases until a package adds them with a low prior.

title: Realism baseline for the renderer as it stands, with devices and the live lab render paths
summary: Captures and scores the renderer as it stands, records what the seven renderer and harness files edited after the last scorecard changed (HANDOVER 6.1), adds PCI device scenes (guide, wire, balloon, stent) and the diagnostic and PCI lab render paths to the capture set, and stores the result as the reference every renderer-editing package is compared with. Improving realism itself is a separate track (section 8).
tipIntegration: None.
lessonAndCaseLinks: None.
design: src/dev/xrayCapture.ts gains capture specs that draw PCI devices through pciDevices from src/ui/sections/AngioPci.tsx (guide in the left main, wire across the LAD lesion, balloon inflated in the lesion, stent deployed), and a live-path mode that films one sequence through the diagnostic lab's scene assembly (FluoroView.tsx 115-205) and one through the PCI lab's (AngioPci.tsx around 826), so the scorecard measures what the trainee sees rather than the capture path alone (xrayCapture.ts around 206). The current code is captured with the c1g0 specs and scored with scripts/realism/report.py; the result is stored as the set 'baseline' and written to docs/realism/baseline.md with the date, the specs, the headline (rows inside the real band out of the total) and the row list. For each of the seven files edited between 22:26 and 22:34 on 5 October (sceneBuilder.ts, thorax.ts, thorax.test.ts, xrayCapture.ts, XrayRenderer.ts, systemProfiles.ts, pyramid.ts), the notes say what the code now does in the areas the scorecard measures and which rows moved against c1g0 (186 of 236, compare_sets.py c1g0 baseline); where a change cannot be reconstructed from the code and the existing notes, the notes say so. Device and live-path rows have no real reference band yet: report.py records them as measurements and leaves them out of the pass count until licensed reference runs exist. No renderer constant changes in this package. Later packages compare with python3 scripts/realism/compare_sets.py baseline <set>.

title: Patient engine formulary, interactions, heparin kinetics and the contrast ceiling
summary: Every drug, route, infusion and interaction the PCI, diagnostic, full-case and physiology plans add to the shared PatientEngine, in one change, plus one contrast-ceiling module used by all labs. Merges proc-engine-formulary with the drug additions of pci-antithrombotic-orders, diag-lab-drugs and diag-contrast-ceilings-oedema, the heparin half-life recalibration from proc-heparin-act-handover, the PDE-5 interaction from proc-chart-planted-problems and diag-lab-drugs, and the contrast ceiling from pci-budgets-stop-rules. It is the only package that adds drugs; later packages call giveDrug and do not edit pharmacology.ts.
tipIntegration: None directly. The engine's new states (over-sedation, desaturation, pulmonary oedema, reaction components) feed found-lab-session-plumbing's patientEvents.
lessonAndCaseLinks: None; consumers link.
design: pharmacology.ts DrugId adds flumazenil, naloxone, diazepam, propofol, dobutamine, dopamine, vasopressin, isoprenaline, furosemide, salbutamol (route 'neb'), amiodarone, IV lidocaine, metoprolol, flecainide, nicardipine, aminophylline, eptifibatide, tirofiban, cangrelor, bivalirudin, idarucizumab, andexanet alfa, prothrombin complex concentrate, nitroprusside (intracoronary route with a systemic hypotension effect), and the oral antiplatelets aspirin, clopidogrel, prasugrel and ticagrelor (oral and crushed routes, loading and maintenance doses, onset curves labelled as model parameters, and an effect on the thrombus and stent-thrombosis hazards); InfusionOrder widens to phenylephrine, adrenaline, dobutamine, dopamine, vasopressin, cangrelor, a GP IIb/IIIa inhibitor and bivalirudin. Each dose and threshold carries a source location from the module text, or a MODEL PARAMETER label in docs/realism/facts/S9.md (HANDOVER 6.4: about 150 dose statements are unaudited, so no value from memory). Effects: antithrombotic effect enters actTrue and the thrombus hazard; dobutamine inotropy and chronotropy; vasopressin and phenylephrine vasoconstriction; furosemide venodilation then diuresis; salbutamol relieves the airway component of a reaction (responses.ts splits reactions into skin, airway and circulation components); flumazenil and naloxone reverse midazolam and fentanyl in titrated steps; oxygen as an FiO2 term in the SpO2 target; a dynamic LVOT obstruction factor for an obstructive HCM profile; IV adrenaline 1 mg with a pulse gives severe hypertension or VT; an interaction table (PDE-5 inhibitor within its window multiplies nitrate vasodilation; a nitrate infusion blunts a bolus; long QT, pre-excitation, high-grade block and poor LV flag antiarrhythmics). Heparin: recalibrate heparinHalfLifeS so a 25 U/kg bolus gives about 30 min and 100 U/kg about 60 min, as the lesson states (now about 47 and 74 min). engine.rightHeart() returns RA, PCWP (from LVEDP), CO and SVR. New src/simulation/patient/contrastBudget.ts: ceilings by Brilakis 3.7 x GFR (3.7 x CrCl in CTO) and the Oxford mL/kg rule, minus recent contrast, with the warning threshold (default 80% of the stricter ceiling) and announcement points (50% and 100%) as labelled model parameters; every lab reads it. team/params.ts (QUERY_ABOVE, DRUG_ROLE), team/intents.ts (DRUG_ALIASES) and team/roles/drugs.ts include every new DrugId, or typecheck fails.

Distal perforation: second wire and microcatheter beside the blocking balloon in one guide with minimum guide size per microcatheter (Brilakis Table 26.2); coil size and compatibility (0.014 or 0.018 lumen); the fat-embolisation option. title: Manifold air, coronary air embolism, diagnostic-catheter dissection and embolic stroke
summary: A table set-up step where the manifold may hold a bubble or a loose connection, with coronary air embolism on the first injection if missed; ostial dissection from injecting through an abnormal trace, with the manual's choices including hand-over to the PCI lab; and embolic stroke from flushing a plugged catheter.

design: TableView set-up: the scenario places a bubble in the contrast port, pressure line, dome or syringe, or a loose connection; the learner inspects (zoom shows the bubble), flushes, runs contrast through and zeros; the syringe must be tip-down for injection. A missed bubble sets airPendingMl in a stand-alone case so labSession.embolise runs; sceneBuilder renders an air lucency in the distal branch (never in normal runs). Choices: store the loop, oxygen, aspirate through the catheter, a wire through the bubbles, IC nitrate, observe. Dissection: an injection with tipState damped or ventricularised, or a deep tip, sets an ostial dissection with probability (model parameter); contrastTransport retains a linear stain on later runs. Choices: stop injecting, retract, wire through the diagnostic catheter, second access and guide (hand-over to the PCI lab with the dissection through found-handover-contract), or oxygen, analgesia, IC nitrate and transfer. Stroke: a flush into a plugged catheter gives a focal deficit; correct actions stop, stroke team and CT with CTA, with heparin noted. A session module src/ui/sim/modules/iatrogenic.ts holds the set-up state.
acceptance: An unflushed scenario bubble gives airEmbolisms 1 on the first selective injection in a stand-alone case; flushing first gives 0

title: Pre-procedure drug orders: anticoagulants, antiplatelets, kidney protection
summary: A scored pre-procedure order sheet: oral anticoagulant hold, continue or bridge with restart time; aspirin and P2Y12 choice, load and timing with contraindication screening; saline, metformin, NSAID and statin orders for a low-eGFR patient with a stated contrast ceiling.

lessonAndCaseLinks: Scenarios oac-af-low-risk, oac-mechanical-valve, oac-rheumatic-mitral, oac-lv-thrombus, warfarin-inr-high, elective-pci-preload, nste-early-angio, stemi-opioids, ckd-egfr-28-metformin-nsaid and ckd-low-ef.
design: src/simulation/session/preorders.ts: OAC hold durations by drug and clearance (Brilakis Table 1.2, Oxford 24 h, 72 h dabigatran in renal impairment); warfarin 5 days or 3-5 days; no routine bridging in AF (BRIDGE); bridging for a mechanical or other prosthetic valve, rheumatic mitral disease and non-laminar thrombus; restart time required. Antiplatelets: clopidogrel for stable disease or with an OAC; prasugrel or ticagrelor for ACS; elective preload clopidogrel 600 mg ideally 6 h or more before; no routine NSTE pretreatment before early angiography; STEMI before or at PCI; opioid-delayed absorption leads to an IV agent; contraindication flags (stroke or TIA, ICH, age over 75, weight under 60 kg, strong CYP3A drugs, high-dose simvastatin or lovastatin). Antiplatelet preload orders call giveDrug with the oral or crushed route, so the onset curves from found-patient-formulary set the antiplatelet effect and the thrombus hazard when the case starts; they are not chart-only.

title: Micropuncture upsizing, sheath preparation and the femoral angiogram
summary: Upsizing from the micropuncture wire to a 0.035 wire, a safe skin nick, sheath length, aspiration and flushing with separate syringes, upsizing resistance, then a femoral angiogram in the ipsilateral oblique with a structured report.

design: src/simulation/access/upsizing.ts state machine: needle out over the 0.018 wire, micropuncture dilator in, inner dilator and wire out, 0.035 J in, dilator out, skin nick (over needle or dilator; blocked with a sheath in), sheath 10, 25 or 45 cm. Wire choice at the needle (a polymer-jacketed wire withdrawn through the needle can shear). Sheath preparation for both routes: 'aspirate 3-4 mL and discard' then 'flush with a second syringe'; an unaspirated sheath before the first catheter, and before a guide at the PCI hand-over, sets sheath.clot (found-handover-contract) so the catheter fails to aspirate at the root. Resistance events by script (scar, kinked wire, poor track, 0.035 kinking, a sheath with no arterial waveform = subintimal; injecting through it is critical); forcing any is a ledger failure. Femoral angiogram: sheathPuff gains volume (5-10 mL); AccessFluoroView adds RAO and LAO 20/30 and magnification; femoralAngioTubes draws the IEA and true puncture height, with SFA and PFA overlapping in AP and separating only in the ipsilateral oblique; a structured report (above or below the bifurcation, relation to the IEA, size above or below 5 mm, disease) is graded and stored as femoralAngioReport for closure.

title: Anaphylaxis order set and vasovagal look-alikes at puncture, sheath and removal
summary: An anaphylaxis event treated through orders with consequences for wrong orders, a vasovagal look-alike and a pre-arrest bradycardic anaphylaxis variant, and vagal prevention and management at puncture, sheath insertion and removal.

Random-case reaction incidence must not change.

summary: Replaces instant bench inflations with indeflator.ts and the lesion-yield model from pci-indeflator: waists yield over pressure and time, rupture follows the drawn burst pressure, fast inflation melon-seeds, cutting balloons have a rate and pressure rule, lithotripsy has an emitter field and pulse counter; adds very-high-pressure balloons, buddy wires and an uncrossable or undilatable mode. IVL energy falls off about 3 mm from each emitter, so a coverage map shows untreated length; the pulse limit (80, Brilakis Fig. 30.89) is data with its citation. design: catalogue.ts takes PCI ladder bases from each definition's epa (new bifurcation, LM and graft bases map to existing EPAs unless progress/types gains EPAs) and builds held-out exam variants (prefix X) that never equal practice variants; it adds the other labs' heldOut preset ids to their EPA ladders and isExamCase. standards.ts gains PCI critical errors (perforation, unrecognised dissection, wire exit with a device advanced over it, contrast above 3.7 x CrCl) that reset the count, plus measured standards from pciMetrics. competency.ts lets PCI, haemo-cath, mcs-support, structural and bedside EPAs reach III and IV after the agreed number of distinct exam passes on two days without a critical error, with expiry dropping a level. Level labels and the standards rule for diagnostic levels III and IV come from progression-labels. logbook.ts records role, access, presentation, complexity, techniques and complications. visibility.ts treats leaving an exam as a failure. Challenge.tsx lists lab exams. Thresholds are simulator defaults (standards.ts source simDefault), not validated, and say so; build at least two held-out cases per rung before enabling.
acceptance: progress.test.ts: two exam passes on distinct held-out variants on two days with no critical error raise pci-simple and haemo-cath to III; a perforation resets the PCI count; expiry drops a level
Exam variants never equal practice variants; a practice session on a held-out id is rejected
The logbook entry has all Oxford fields

title: Point the existing lesson and case blocks at their P1 scenarios
summary: Converts the existing sim and drill blocks (84 angio-pci drill blocks, 108 cathlab and 94 procedure sim blocks, and the dev-lab sim blocks) whose scenarios come from P1 packages to explicit launch params, and adds CaseStudy.practice links, following each lab request's lessonIds, so the inline blocks open the right scenario as well as the practice index. Merges pci-lesson-deeplink-backfill and proc-content-deeplinks and adds the cathlab and dev-lab links the other plans left implicit.
tipIntegration: None. A warning check flags links whose lesson has tips that the linked scenario cannot raise (from the reachability lists).
lessonAndCaseLinks: practiceIndex has listed each scenario under its lessons and cases since the scenario's .launch.ts landed. This package makes the inline sim and drill blocks agree with it for P1 scenarios; content-links-backfill-p2 and content-links-backfill-p3 do the same for P2 and P3 scenarios.
design: A small node script (run with vite-node, not committed output) lists sim and drill blocks per lab with their lesson ids, the lab requests' lessonIds and the practiceIndex entries; the author maps them to scenario ids and edits the manual files and src/content/cases/published.ts by hand. Passes in order: PCI, procedure and access, cathlab, then the dev labs. content.test.ts gains: every drill block with target 'angio-pci' and every sim block for cathlab and procedure whose scenario exists has a scenario param that validateLaunchLinks accepts, and every lessonId named by a P1 lab request appears in practiceIndex or has a block whose scenario lists that lesson. Runs alone after tip-retarget-catchup, because both edit the same module files. Added after build run 3 (from builders' out-of-scope reports, docs/curriculum/lab-reports/run3/): (a) The four sim blocks in src/content/manual/complex-pci/03-bifurcation-two-stent.ts marked 'POT practice only' can now link the bifurcation bench presets, for example {preset:'bif-dk-crush', start:'crush'} and {preset:'bif-tap', start:'set-protrusion'}. (b) src/content/manual/cath-handbook/08-mitral-tricuspid-laa.ts, the TEER and LAAO sim blocks of lesson ts-setup: the task text still says 'Drag the needle tip on the fossa map'; describe the hands-on pull-down built by structural-transseptal-hands-on.
acceptance: content.test.ts: every angio-pci drill block and every cathlab and procedure sim block whose scenario comes from a P1 package has a scenario param that validateLaunchLinks accepts
Every lessonId named by a P1 lab request in docs/curriculum/lab-requests/*.json appears in practiceIndex or has a block whose scenario lists that lesson
The link-to-tips warning count is reported and recorded in the package notes
browser: three sampled lessons per lab open the lab on their named scenario, from the inline block and from 'Practise this in the lab'

title: Link lessons to the P3 scenarios
summary: A short second pass of content-links-backfill for the scenarios that the P3 packages add, so the link test can cover every lab request.
tipIntegration: None.
lessonAndCaseLinks: Adds launch params for the P3 scenarios (SCAD, serial lesions, TAVI PCI, septal ablation, guide extension, septal occluder, valvuloplasty, biopsy, support standby, sterile field, supervisor mode) to the lessons their requests name.
design: Same method as content-links-backfill, limited to the lessons named by P3 requests. The content test's request-coverage check is extended from P1 and P2 to all requests, counting practiceIndex entries as links.
acceptance: content.test.ts: every lessonId named by any lab request has at least one block whose scenario lists that lesson
validateLaunchLinks accepts every new param
